claims.claim: Episode opens on morning of 16 June 1904
claims.evidence: '16 June 1904' appears in text (Ithaca/ catechism, and Mulligan morning scene)

claims.claim: At a Martello tower near Dublin
claims.evidence: 'Martello you call it?' (line 850); 'I want Sandycove milk'; 'this tower'

claims.claim: Mulligan shaves on the roof and mocks Stephen
claims.evidence: 'Stately, plump Buck Mulligan ... bearing a bowl of lather'

claims.claim: Mulligan is a medical student
claims.evidence: 'Are you a medical student, sir?' 'I am, ma'am'

claims.claim: Stephen lodges at the tower with the Englishman Haines
claims.evidence: 'How long is Haines going to stay in this tower?'; Haines in the livingroom

claims.claim: Stephen is a young teacher haunted by his mother's death
claims.evidence: 'Whose mother is beastly dead'; 'Mr Deasy is calling you'; 'Mother's deathbed'

claims.claim: Stephen leaves the tower, teaches at Mr Deasy's school
claims.evidence: school scene, 'Mr Deasy told me to write them out'

claims.claim: Stephen walks the strand
claims.evidence: Proteus chapter

claims.claim: Bloom is a Jewish advertising canvasser
claims.evidence: 'He does some canvassing for ads'; 'Why will you jews not accept our culture'

claims.claim: Bloom makes breakfast for wife Molly
claims.evidence: 'breakfast things on the humpy tray ... She didn't like her plate full'

claims.claim: Bloom attends Paddy Dignam's funeral
claims.evidence: 'Poor Dignam! His last lie on the earth in his box'; Dignam among those in bed/ the grave

claims.claim: Bloom knows Molly will meet lover Boylan that afternoon
claims.evidence: 'At four she.' 'Who said four?'; Boylan: 'What time is that? Four?'

claims.claim: Bloom finds drunken Stephen in brothel quarter
claims.evidence: Nighttown, Mabbot Street entrance; Bella Cohen

claims.claim: Bloom takes Stephen home to Eccles Street
claims.evidence: Eccles street; Ithaca catechism 'temporary guest'

claims.claim: Stephen leaves
claims.evidence: 'How did they take leave ... in separation?'

claims.claim: Bloom goes to bed beside Molly
claims.evidence: 'entered the bed' (Ithaca)

claims.claim: Molly's thoughts close the book with 'yes I will Yes'
claims.evidence: final line 'I said yes I will Yes.'

claims.claim: Molly is a singer
claims.evidence: 'Madame Marion Tweedy ... the soprano'

claims.claim: Boylan is a concert manager
claims.evidence: searched Boylan/manager/impresario; text only shows him 'mixed up' in the tour
claims.fix: a jaunty Dubliner mixed up in her concert tour

claims.claim: Bloom's hearing: Molly will meet Boylan at four ('knowing')
claims.evidence: as above

claims.claim: Dignam is the dead man whose funeral Bloom attends
claims.evidence: as above
